questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Invoices sub-tab Sales section
questions.text: The Sales section in QuickBooks Online has five sub-tabs. Which sub-tab shows a list focused on invoice transactions specifically?

answers.text: Invoices
All Sales
Customers
Products and Services

explanations.a: The Student Guide lists Invoices as one of the five Sales sub-tabs; clicking it filters the transaction list to show invoice transactions.
explanations.b: All Sales shows every sales-related transaction type combined, not just invoices.
explanations.c: The Customers sub-tab shows a list of customer records, not individual invoice transactions.
explanations.d: Products and Services shows the items list, not sales transactions.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Save and send email invoice immediately
questions.text: After completing an invoice in QuickBooks Online, a bookkeeper wants to save it and send it to the customer by email in one step. Which save option accomplishes this?

answers.text: Save and close
Save and send
Save and new
Save

explanations.a: Save and close saves the invoice and closes the form but does not send an email to the customer.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states Save and send saves the invoice and immediately sends it to the customer by email.
explanations.c: Save and new saves the invoice and opens a blank new invoice form; it does not send an email to the customer.
explanations.d: Save saves the invoice without sending it and keeps the current form open for further editing.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Sales Receipt immediate payment no AR balance
questions.text: A coffee shop collects payment from customers at the counter at the moment of purchase. Which QuickBooks Online transaction type is appropriate for this scenario and why?

answers.text: Invoice, because it records the revenue and payment in a single step for quick service businesses.
Receive Payment, because it immediately applies cash to the customer's balance.
Sales Receipt, because the customer pays immediately at the time of sale and no accounts receivable balance is created.
Estimate, because it records what the customer agreed to pay before the transaction is finalized.

explanations.a: An Invoice creates an Accounts Receivable balance that must be separately paid; it is not the right tool when payment is collected immediately.
explanations.b: Receive Payment requires an existing open invoice to apply against; it is not the starting transaction for immediate point-of-sale payments.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states Sales Receipts are used when customers pay immediately at the time of the sale, and unlike invoices, they do not create an Accounts Receivable balance.
explanations.d: An Estimate is a non-posting quote; it does not record a completed sale.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Credit Memo reduce balance customer return
questions.text: A customer returns a product and expects a reduction in the amount they owe on their account. Which QuickBooks Online transaction is used to record this?

answers.text: Refund Receipt, which records money returned to the customer from the company's bank account.
Delayed Credit, which holds the credit as a non-posting reminder for a future invoice.
Vendor Credit, which records a credit received from the vendor for the returned product.
Credit Memo, which reduces the amount the customer owes on an existing or future invoice.

explanations.a: A Refund Receipt is used when cash is physically returned to the customer; a Credit Memo reduces a balance without necessarily issuing a cash refund.
explanations.b: Delayed Credit is a non-posting transaction that does not affect the current AR balance; it is not used to record a completed return.
explanations.c: Vendor Credit records credits from vendors, not adjustments to customer accounts.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states Credit Memos are used to reduce the amount owed by a customer on an existing invoice or to apply against a future invoice.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: estimate non-posting no accounting entry general ledger
questions.text: A salesperson creates an estimate in QuickBooks Online for a potential client. What effect does creating the estimate have on the company's financial records?

answers.text: None — estimates are non-posting transactions and have no effect on the general ledger.
It debits Accounts Receivable and credits Sales for the estimated amount.
It creates a pending revenue entry that posts automatically when the customer accepts.
It increases a Sales Pipeline balance in the Chart of Accounts until converted to an invoice.

explanations.a: The Student Guide states estimates are non-posting transactions; they do not create any accounting entries in the general ledger.
explanations.b: Accounts Receivable is only affected when an invoice (a posting transaction) is created; estimates do not debit AR.
explanations.c: Estimates remain non-posting even after a customer accepts; an invoice must be created to generate a posting entry.
explanations.d: There is no Sales Pipeline account in QBO's Chart of Accounts; estimates leave no accounting footprint.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Delayed Charge non-posting billable reminder hold charges
questions.text: A bookkeeper records materials used at a customer's job site but is not ready to invoice the customer yet. Which transaction type holds these charges as a non-posting reminder until invoicing?

answers.text: Credit Memo
Delayed Charge
Sales Receipt
Estimate

explanations.a: A Credit Memo reduces a customer's AR balance; it is not used to hold pending charges for future invoicing.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states Delayed Charges are non-posting transactions used to hold charges incurred for a customer as a reminder to invoice them at a later date.
explanations.c: A Sales Receipt records immediate payment and is not used to hold pending charges for later invoicing.
explanations.d: An Estimate is a quote for future work; it is not used to hold charges for work already performed that will be billed later.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: five Sales sub-tabs Overview All Sales Invoices Customers Products
questions.text: The Sales section in QuickBooks Online contains five sub-tabs. Which set correctly lists all five?

answers.text: Overview, Invoices, Estimates, Customers, Payments.
Overview, All Sales, Invoices, Payments, Products and Services.
Overview, All Sales, Invoices, Customers, Products and Services.
Overview, All Sales, Invoices, Estimates, Customers.

explanations.a: Estimates and Payments are not the correct fifth and fourth sub-tabs; the correct sub-tabs are Overview, All Sales, Invoices, Customers, and Products and Services.
explanations.b: Payments is not one of the five Sales sub-tabs; Products and Services is correct but replaces Payments.
explanations.c: The Student Guide identifies the five Sales sub-tabs as Overview, All Sales, Invoices, Customers, and Products and Services.
explanations.d: Estimates is not one of the five Sales sub-tabs as described in the Student Guide.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Refund Receipt no AR balance cash returned to customer
questions.text: A customer requests a full cash refund for a returned item and currently has no open invoice balance. Which QuickBooks Online transaction is used to record money being returned to the customer?

answers.text: Credit Memo — apply it to reduce the customer's future invoice.
Receive Payment — apply the refund to the customer's balance.
Delayed Credit — hold the refund as a non-posting credit for future invoicing.
Refund Receipt — used when the customer has no AR balance and cash is being returned directly to them.

explanations.a: A Credit Memo reduces the amount a customer owes; when there is no open balance and cash must physically leave the company, a Refund Receipt is required.
explanations.b: Receive Payment records money coming in from a customer; it cannot be used to record money going out as a refund.
explanations.c: Delayed Credit is non-posting and does not issue a cash refund; it is used to hold a credit for a future invoice.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states a Refund Receipt is used when the customer has no accounts receivable balance and money is being returned to the customer.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Undeposited Funds Receive Payment Deposit to field default
questions.text: When recording a Receive Payment in QuickBooks Online, the Deposit to field has a default that holds all received funds together until they are batched into a single bank deposit. What is this default account called?

answers.text: Undeposited Funds
Cash in Bank
Customer Prepayments
Clearing Account

explanations.a: The Student Guide states the default Deposit to selection in Receive Payment is Undeposited Funds, a holding account used to batch multiple payments into a single deposit that matches the bank statement.
explanations.b: Cash in Bank is not the name of the default holding account; Undeposited Funds is the correct default.
explanations.c: Customer Prepayments is not a QBO default account name for the Deposit to field.
explanations.d: Clearing Account is a generic accounting term; the specific QBO account used for this purpose is Undeposited Funds.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Projects left navigation bar tab separate
questions.text: In QuickBooks Online, the Projects feature allows tracking of income, expenses, and profitability for specific client engagements. Where is the Projects feature located in the navigation?

answers.text: Under Sales → All Sales → filter by Project type.
As a dedicated Projects tab in the left navigation bar.
Under Expenses → Projects sub-tab.
Under the Reports tab, within the By Project report group.

explanations.a: Filtering All Sales by Project type does not lead to the full Projects feature; Projects has its own dedicated navigation tab.
explanations.b: The Student Guide indicates Projects appears as a separate tab in the left navigation bar, giving direct access to the project management functionality.
explanations.c: Projects is not a sub-tab under Expenses; it is a standalone left-navigation tab.
explanations.d: Projects is not accessed through the Reports tab; it has its own dedicated navigation tab.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.4 Receive Payment — sticky Deposit to field warning
questions.keyword: sticky Deposit to field Receive Payment bypasses Undeposited Funds
questions.text: A bookkeeper who normally uses Undeposited Funds switches one Receive Payment to deposit directly to the checking account. The Student Guide warns about a specific risk with this change. What is that risk?

answers.text: Switching the deposit account triggers auto-application of any existing customer credits, causing an overpayment.
The payment will not post to Accounts Receivable, leaving the invoice permanently open.
The Deposit to field is sticky and retains the last-used selection; if the bookkeeper forgets to switch back, future payments may accidentally bypass Undeposited Funds.
QBO prevents direct bank account selection in Receive Payment and requires Undeposited Funds in all cases.

explanations.a: The deposit account selection does not trigger credit auto-application; those are independent settings.
explanations.b: The payment still posts to AR and closes the invoice regardless of which deposit account is selected.
explanations.c: The Student Guide warns that the Deposit to field is sticky — it stays on the last-used selection — so if a bookkeeper changes it for one transaction and forgets to change it back, future payments may inadvertently bypass Undeposited Funds.
explanations.d: QBO does allow selecting a bank account directly in the Deposit to field; it is not restricted to Undeposited Funds.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.5 Sales Receipts — Deposit to field caution
questions.keyword: Sales Receipt Deposit to same sticky field caution
questions.text: A bookkeeper notices the Sales Receipt form has the same Deposit to field as the Receive Payment form. The Student Guide includes a caution for this field on Sales Receipts. What is that caution?

answers.text: Sales Receipts must always use Undeposited Funds; selecting a direct bank account will post revenue to the wrong period.
If Undeposited Funds is selected on a Sales Receipt, a separate Deposit transaction must be created or the funds will never clear the holding account.
Sales Receipts using Undeposited Funds cannot be included in customer statements.
The same sticky Deposit to field caution applies; the bookkeeper should pay attention to which account is selected each time a Sales Receipt is entered.

explanations.a: QBO does not require Sales Receipts to use Undeposited Funds; either a holding account or a direct bank account can be selected.
explanations.b: The Student Guide does not state that funds in Undeposited Funds from Sales Receipts are unrecorded without a deposit; they are held and then combined into a deposit.
explanations.c: There is no restriction on including Undeposited Funds Sales Receipts in customer statements.
explanations.d: The Student Guide notes the same sticky field caution applies to Sales Receipts as to Receive Payments; the bookkeeper should check the Deposit to field every time to ensure the correct account is selected.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Credit Memo auto-apply oldest open invoice
questions.text: A Credit Memo is created for a customer who currently has an open invoice, and the automation setting for auto-applying credits is turned on. What does QuickBooks Online do by default?

answers.text: QBO automatically applies the credit to the oldest open invoice for that customer.
QBO moves the credit to a clearing account until the bookkeeper manually links it to an invoice.
QBO holds the credit as unapplied until the customer calls to request application.
QBO automatically issues a physical check refund to the customer for the credit amount.

explanations.a: The Student Guide states that when auto-applying credits is enabled, QBO automatically applies a Credit Memo to the oldest open invoice for that customer.
explanations.b: Credits are not moved to a clearing account; when auto-apply is on, they are applied directly to an open invoice.
explanations.c: Auto-apply credits does not wait for customer contact; it applies the credit automatically as described in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: QBO does not automatically issue checks; a Refund Receipt is a separate transaction the bookkeeper must intentionally create.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: packing slip Print or Preview dropdown invoice
questions.text: After saving an invoice in QuickBooks Online, a warehouse team needs to print a packing slip for the shipment. Where is the packing slip option found?

answers.text: In the invoice footer, by clicking a dedicated Packing Slip button that appears once the invoice is saved.
In the Print or Preview drop-down at the bottom of the invoice screen, which includes Packing slip as one of the print options.
In the Reports tab under Sales and Customers, by running a Packing Slip report filtered by invoice number.
In the Customer Center by selecting the invoice row and choosing Print → Packing Slip from the action column.

explanations.a: There is no dedicated Packing Slip button in the invoice footer described in the Student Guide; it is accessed through the Print or Preview drop-down.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states the Print or Preview drop-down at the bottom of the invoice screen offers a Packing slip option alongside the standard invoice print option.
explanations.c: A dedicated Packing Slip report in the Report Center is not described as the method in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: The Student Guide does not describe a Print → Packing Slip path from the Customer Center action column.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Delayed Credit non-posting reduce future invoice reminder
questions.text: A bookkeeper wants to give a customer a credit that does not immediately affect Accounts Receivable but will appear as a reminder to apply against a future invoice. Which transaction type fits this need?

answers.text: Credit Memo, because it reduces the customer's current AR balance as soon as it is saved.
Refund Receipt, because it records money physically returned to the customer.
Delayed Credit, which is a non-posting transaction that appears as a reminder to apply to a future invoice.
Vendor Credit, which holds a credit amount until it can be applied to a future vendor payment.

explanations.a: A Credit Memo is a posting transaction that immediately reduces the customer's AR balance; it does not serve as a non-posting reminder.
explanations.b: A Refund Receipt records cash leaving the company to refund a customer; it is not a non-posting reminder.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states Delayed Credits are non-posting transactions used to hold a credit as a reminder so it can be applied to a future customer invoice.
explanations.d: Vendor Credit is a vendor-side transaction for credits received from suppliers; it does not apply to customer accounts.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: estimate Create Invoice button top right convert
questions.text: After a customer verbally accepts an estimate in QuickBooks Online, what is the quickest method to convert the estimate into an invoice?

answers.text: Open a Sales Receipt for the customer and click Estimate at the top right to pull in estimate details.
Use +New → Invoice, then manually re-enter all items from the estimate on the invoice screen.
Open the Estimates sub-tab, select the estimate, and click Copy to Invoice from the action column.
Open the estimate itself and click the Create Invoice button at the top right.

explanations.a: There is no Estimate button on a Sales Receipt screen; Sales Receipts are for immediate payment and are not linked to estimates this way.
explanations.b: Manually re-entering estimate items on a new invoice is unnecessary extra work; QBO provides a direct conversion path.
explanations.c: While the Estimates sub-tab exists in some versions of QBO, the Student Guide points to opening the estimate and using the Create Invoice button as the direct method.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states a user can open the estimate and click Create Invoice in the top right corner to convert it directly to an invoice with all the estimate details pre-populated.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Balance Forward Open Item Transaction List statement types
questions.text: When generating a customer statement in QuickBooks Online, three statement formats are available. Which set correctly names all three?

answers.text: Balance Forward, Open Item, and Transaction List.
Balance Forward, Outstanding Balance, and Overdue Items.
Open Invoice, Paid Invoice, and Credit Balance.
Summary, Detail, and Activity Statement.

explanations.a: The Student Guide identifies the three statement types in QBO as Balance Forward, Open Item, and Transaction List.
explanations.b: Outstanding Balance and Overdue Items are not the names of QBO statement types; the correct three are Balance Forward, Open Item, and Transaction List.
explanations.c: Open Invoice, Paid Invoice, and Credit Balance are not the statement type names listed in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: Summary, Detail, and Activity Statement are not the statement type names described in the Student Guide.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: drawer slides right side billable time expenses delayed charges
questions.text: When creating an invoice for a customer who has pending billable charges, time entries, or delayed charges, how does QuickBooks Online alert the bookkeeper and present those items?

answers.text: A notification email is sent to the bookkeeper listing all open billable charges for the customer.
A drawer slides out on the right side of the invoice screen showing pending billable time, expenses, and delayed charges that can be selectively added.
QBO automatically adds all pending billable charges to the invoice without prompting the bookkeeper to review them.
A pop-up alert appears in the top navigation bar when the customer is selected on the invoice.

explanations.a: QBO does not send emails to bookkeepers about pending billable charges; the notification happens within the invoice screen itself.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states that when a customer has pending billable charges, a drawer slides open on the right side of the invoice screen, allowing the bookkeeper to review and selectively add those charges.
explanations.c: QBO does not automatically add charges to an invoice; the bookkeeper must select which items to include from the drawer.
explanations.d: A pop-up in the top navigation bar is not how QBO surfaces billable charge reminders; the drawer mechanism is used instead.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.1 Customer Center money bar — Unbilled Activity
questions.keyword: Unbilled Activity money bar Customer Center segment
questions.text: In the Customer Center money bar, one colored segment represents customer activity that has been incurred but not yet invoiced. What is this segment called?

answers.text: Open Estimates.
Pending Invoices.
Unbilled Activity.
Deferred Revenue.

explanations.a: Open Estimates is not the name of the money bar segment for uninvoiced charges; the correct label is Unbilled Activity.
explanations.b: Pending Invoices is not the money bar segment label described in the Student Guide for uninvoiced amounts.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states the Unbilled Activity segment in the Customer Center money bar represents charges that have been recorded but not yet included on an invoice sent to the customer.
explanations.d: Deferred Revenue is an accounting concept for advance payments received; it is not the name of a Customer Center money bar segment.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: batch three checks single deposit transaction bank statement line
questions.text: A bookkeeper received three customer checks on the same day and recorded each using Receive Payment into Undeposited Funds. What is the next step, and why is this workflow used?

answers.text: QBO automatically combines the three payments into a single bank deposit with no further action required.
Each payment must be deposited individually with three separate Deposit transactions to match three separate bank lines.
The bookkeeper must close and reopen QBO for the Undeposited Funds balance to transfer to the bank account.
The bookkeeper creates one Deposit transaction selecting all three payments, producing a single deposit that matches the single line on the bank statement.

explanations.a: QBO does not automatically move funds from Undeposited Funds to the bank; a Deposit transaction must be created by the bookkeeper.
explanations.b: Creating three separate deposits would produce three bank lines, making it harder to match the single combined deposit line on the bank statement.
explanations.c: Closing and reopening QBO has no effect on the Undeposited Funds balance; a Deposit transaction is required.
explanations.d: The Student Guide explains that using Undeposited Funds allows a bookkeeper to batch multiple payments into a single Deposit transaction that mirrors the single deposit line that appears on the bank statement, making reconciliation easier.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.4 Receive Payment — applying to a specific invoice
questions.keyword: check checkbox specific invoice Receive Payment apply
questions.text: A customer has two open invoices but sends a payment that covers only one of them. How does the bookkeeper ensure the payment is applied to the correct invoice in the Receive Payment screen?

answers.text: Check the checkbox next to the specific invoice being paid and leave the other invoice unchecked.
QBO applies all payments to the oldest open invoice first and this behavior cannot be changed without a credit memo.
Enter two separate Receive Payment transactions, one per invoice, splitting the amount between them.
Close the payment window and apply the payment manually through a journal entry referencing the specific invoice.

explanations.a: The Student Guide describes checking the checkbox next to the specific invoice the payment is being applied to in the Receive Payment screen; unchecked invoices remain open.
explanations.b: QBO does not lock payment application to the oldest invoice; the bookkeeper controls which invoices are checked and paid.
explanations.c: Creating two separate Receive Payment transactions for a single customer payment would split the record unnecessarily; one payment applies to one or more invoices via checkboxes.
explanations.d: Journal entries for routine payment application are not standard practice in QBO; the Receive Payment checkbox method handles this.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.14 AR consequences — Deposit instead of Receive Payment
questions.keyword: Deposit instead of Receive Payment AR overstated invoice stays open
questions.text: A bookkeeper records a customer's check as a Deposit transaction (coded directly to an income account) instead of using Receive Payment. What accounting problem does this create?

answers.text: The income account is credited twice, overstating revenue on the Profit and Loss.
The original invoice remains open, overstating Accounts Receivable on the balance sheet.
The checking account is debited twice, overstating the cash balance.
The customer's credit balance becomes negative, triggering an automatic refund from QBO.

explanations.a: The income account is credited only once through the Deposit; revenue is not doubled, but the open invoice inflates AR.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states that using a Deposit instead of Receive Payment leaves the original invoice open, which overstates Accounts Receivable on the balance sheet because the invoice has not been properly closed.
explanations.c: The checking account is correctly debited once by the Deposit transaction; there is no double-debit to cash.
explanations.d: QBO does not trigger automatic refunds; the consequence is an AR overstatement, not a customer credit issue.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Save and new opens blank invoice form next entry
questions.text: When completing an invoice in QuickBooks Online, four save options are available. Which description correctly explains what the Save and new option does?

answers.text: Saves the current invoice, emails it to the customer, and then opens a blank invoice form.
Saves the current invoice and returns the user to the Sales Overview page.
Saves the current invoice and immediately opens a blank invoice form ready for the next entry.
Saves the current invoice as a pending draft and marks it awaiting customer approval.

explanations.a: Save and new does not send an email; Save and send is the option that emails the invoice after saving.
explanations.b: Returning to the Sales Overview after saving is what Save and close does, not Save and new.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states Save and new saves the current invoice and opens a blank new invoice form, enabling the bookkeeper to continue entering the next invoice without navigating away.
explanations.d: Save and new does not create a draft pending approval; it saves the invoice and opens a fresh form immediately.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.6 Credit Memos — manually applying when auto-apply is off
questions.keyword: Receive Payment zero amount credit memo link invoice manually
questions.text: A credit memo was created while auto-apply credits was turned off, leaving the credit unapplied. How does the bookkeeper manually apply the credit to an open invoice?

answers.text: Delete and re-enter the credit memo with auto-apply temporarily turned on to force application.
Create a new invoice with a negative line item to offset the credit memo balance.
In the Chart of Accounts, find the credit memo entry and use the link icon to connect it to the invoice entry.
Open a Receive Payment for the customer, set the amount received to $0.00, then check both the credit memo and the invoice to link them.

explanations.a: Deleting and re-entering a credit memo is destructive to the audit trail; the proper method is to use Receive Payment with a $0 amount.
explanations.b: Creating a new invoice with a negative line item does not properly link the existing credit memo to an open invoice.
explanations.c: The Chart of Accounts does not provide a visual linking tool for credit memos and invoices.
explanations.d: The Student Guide describes opening a Receive Payment for the customer, entering $0.00 as the amount, and then checking both the credit memo and the target invoice so QBO links them and marks both as closed.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.10 Drawer — Add, Open, Add all, Filter by
questions.keyword: drawer options Add Open Add all Filter by billable items
questions.text: When the drawer opens on the right side of an invoice screen to show pending billable items, which set of options is available for managing those items within the drawer?

answers.text: Add, Open, Add all, and a Filter by drop-down.
Apply, Dismiss, Apply all, and a Sort by drop-down.
Accept, Decline, Accept all, and a Group by drop-down.
Include, Exclude, Include all, and a Search by drop-down.

explanations.a: The Student Guide lists the drawer options as Add (add a single item to the invoice), Open (open the source transaction), Add all (add everything in the drawer), and a Filter by drop-down to narrow items by type.
explanations.b: Apply, Dismiss, Apply all, and Sort by are not the option labels described in the Student Guide for the invoice drawer.
explanations.c: Accept, Decline, Accept all, and Group by are not the option labels described in the Student Guide for the invoice drawer.
explanations.d: Include, Exclude, Include all, and Search by are not the option labels described in the Student Guide for the invoice drawer.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: progress invoicing percentage line item remaining balance options
questions.text: When Progress Invoicing is enabled and a bookkeeper is creating a progress invoice from an estimate, which options are available for determining how much to invoice at each stage?

answers.text: Only a percentage of the estimate total can be selected; dollar amounts per line are not available.
The bookkeeper can invoice a percentage of the total estimate, a custom amount or percentage per line item, or the remaining balance.
Progress invoicing always divides the estimate into equal installments based on a number the bookkeeper specifies upfront.
The first progress invoice must be for the full estimate amount; subsequent invoices handle change orders only.

explanations.a: A custom per-line amount or percentage is available in addition to an overall percentage; this option is not restricted to a single total percentage.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states that when creating a progress invoice, the bookkeeper can choose to invoice a percentage of the entire estimate, a custom amount or percentage per line item, or the remaining outstanding balance.
explanations.c: Progress invoicing does not force equal installments; the bookkeeper controls the amount at each stage.
explanations.d: The first progress invoice can be for any portion of the estimate, not necessarily the full amount.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.11 Deposits — Add New Deposits section caution
questions.keyword: Add New Deposits caution income without customer record reporting gap
questions.text: When creating a bank deposit from Undeposited Funds in QuickBooks Online, the deposit screen includes a section for adding new lines at the bottom. The Student Guide warns against using this section carelessly. Why?

answers.text: Lines added at the bottom duplicate existing payments, causing invoices to be overpaid.
Lines added at the bottom default to the cash account, bypassing sales tax calculations.

Adding income lines directly to the deposit rather than using the proper sales workflow posts revenue without creating a customer record or invoice, which can cause gaps in customer and sales reporting.
Lines added at the bottom must match an existing downloaded bank feed transaction exactly or QBO will automatically reverse them.

explanations.a: Lines added at the bottom do not duplicate existing payments from Undeposited Funds; they are separate additional entries.
explanations.b: Default account coding at the bottom of the deposit form does not specifically bypass sales tax; the broader issue is the reporting gap.
explanations.c: The Student Guide warns that entering income amounts directly in the Add funds to this deposit section bypasses the invoice/sales receipt workflow, posting revenue without a customer record or proper sales form, which leads to gaps in accounts receivable and customer reporting.
explanations.d: Lines added to the deposit form do not need to match bank feed downloads; QBO does not automatically reverse them.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.12 Statements — batch creating for multiple customers
questions.keyword: Customers sub-tab Batch Actions Create statements multiple
questions.text: A bookkeeper needs to send monthly statements to multiple overdue customers at once. What is the efficient method for generating these statements in QuickBooks Online?

answers.text: Open each customer's profile individually and use New transaction → Statement for each one.
Go to Reports → Collections Report and click Send Statement next to each customer name.
In the Invoices sub-tab, select all overdue invoices and click Email to customers.
In the Customers sub-tab, select multiple customers using checkboxes, then choose Create statements from the Batch Actions drop-down.

explanations.a: Opening each customer profile individually and creating statements one at a time is inefficient; the batch method exists for this purpose.
explanations.b: The Collections Report does not have a Send Statement button next to each customer; statements are generated from the Customers sub-tab.
explanations.c: Emailing invoices from the Invoices sub-tab does not produce statements; statements are a separate transaction type created through the Customers sub-tab.
explanations.d: The Student Guide describes selecting multiple customers in the Customers sub-tab using checkboxes and then choosing Create statements from the Batch Actions drop-down to generate statements for all selected customers at once.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.8 Delayed Charges — reminder on invoice screen
questions.keyword: Delayed Charge drawer reminder slides open invoice screen
questions.text: When a bookkeeper opens a new invoice for a customer who has pending Delayed Charges, what mechanism does QuickBooks Online use to remind the bookkeeper to include those charges?

answers.text: A drawer slides open on the right side of the invoice screen showing the pending Delayed Charges, which can be added to the invoice.
A pop-up window appears before the invoice screen opens, listing all pending Delayed Charges for the customer.
The Delayed Charges are automatically added to the invoice and must be manually removed if not needed.
The Customer Center money bar turns red before the invoice is opened to indicate pending Delayed Charges.

explanations.a: The Student Guide states that when a customer has pending Delayed Charges (or other billable items), a drawer slides open on the right side of the invoice screen, presenting those charges for the bookkeeper to selectively add.
explanations.b: QBO uses the drawer mechanism within the invoice screen, not a pre-invoice pop-up window, to surface pending charges.
explanations.c: Delayed Charges are not automatically added; the bookkeeper must intentionally select them from the drawer.
explanations.d: The money bar color does not change to alert bookkeepers about pending Delayed Charges; the drawer within the invoice screen is the notification mechanism.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Sales Receipt no AR balance payment at time of sale
questions.text: A retail store records all walk-in purchases using Sales Receipts in QuickBooks Online. How does this differ from using an Invoice in terms of Accounts Receivable?

answers.text: Sales Receipts increase Accounts Receivable temporarily, which is cleared when the bank deposit is created.
Sales Receipts do not create an Accounts Receivable balance because payment is received at the time of the sale.
Sales Receipts create a negative Accounts Receivable balance to reflect advance payment collected.
Sales Receipts bypass all general ledger posting and are stored only in the Customer Center.

explanations.a: Sales Receipts do not create an AR balance; they record both the revenue and the payment simultaneously without going through AR.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states Sales Receipts are used when payment is collected at the time of the sale, and unlike invoices, they do not create an Accounts Receivable balance.
explanations.c: Sales Receipts do not create a negative AR balance; they simply do not affect AR at all.
explanations.d: Sales Receipts are fully posting transactions that affect revenue and cash accounts; they are not bypassed from the general ledger.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: All Sales sub-tab all transaction types combined invoices receipts credits
questions.text: A manager asks what information is visible in the All Sales sub-tab of the Sales section in QuickBooks Online. Which description is accurate?

answers.text: All Sales shows only open, unpaid invoices filtered by overdue status.
All Sales shows only posted transactions and excludes estimates and delayed charges.
All Sales displays every sales-related transaction type including invoices, sales receipts, credit memos, payments, estimates, delayed charges, and delayed credits.
All Sales shows combined customer and vendor transactions for the current fiscal period.

explanations.a: All Sales is not limited to overdue invoices; it shows all sales transaction types regardless of status.
explanations.b: All Sales includes non-posting transaction types such as estimates and delayed charges; it is not limited to posted transactions.
explanations.c: The Student Guide describes the All Sales sub-tab as showing every sales-related transaction type for customers, including invoices, sales receipts, credit memos, payments received, estimates, delayed charges, and delayed credits.
explanations.d: All Sales shows only customer-side transactions; vendor transactions are visible in the Vendor Center and Expenses tab.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Customer name required field invoice cannot save
questions.text: A bookkeeper attempts to save an invoice in QuickBooks Online but receives a validation error. Which of the following is a required field that, if left blank, would prevent the invoice from being saved?

answers.text: The Invoice Date field — QBO requires the date to be typed even when a default is pre-filled.
The Due Date field — it must always be at least one day after the Invoice Date.
The Terms field — a payment term must be selected before an invoice can be saved.
The Customer name field — an invoice cannot be saved without a customer selected.

explanations.a: The Invoice Date is pre-filled automatically and QBO does not block saving if it is filled; a missing customer is more fundamental.
explanations.b: The Due Date field may be calculated from Terms or left based on defaults; it does not independently block saving in the way a missing customer does.
explanations.c: The Terms field has a default and is not strictly required to be manually set before saving an invoice.
explanations.d: The Student Guide confirms that a customer must be selected on an invoice; without a customer in the Customer name field, the invoice cannot be saved.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.12 Statements — Transaction List type use case
questions.keyword: Transaction List statement individual transactions date range
questions.text: A customer questions a charge from three months ago that appeared on a Balance Forward statement. The bookkeeper wants to send a statement showing every individual invoice and payment for the past 90 days in detail. Which statement type should be used?

answers.text: Transaction List, which shows all individual transactions within a specified date range for the customer.
Open Item, which shows all open invoices and unapplied credits but excludes fully paid transactions.
Balance Forward, which carries over prior balances and shows new charges for the selected period only.
Activity Statement, which shows all activity across all customers combined for the specified period.

explanations.a: The Student Guide describes the Transaction List statement type as showing all individual transactions (invoices, payments, credits) for the customer within a specified date range, making it ideal for detailed dispute resolution.
explanations.b: Open Item shows current unpaid balances; it excludes paid transactions which may be needed to explain the disputed charge.
explanations.c: Balance Forward carries over a prior balance as a single line rather than showing each transaction in detail; it is the type that created the confusion in the scenario.
explanations.d: Activity Statement is not a QBO statement type described in the Student Guide; the three types are Balance Forward, Open Item, and Transaction List.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Filter by drawer narrow items type Time Expenses Delayed Charges
questions.text: Multiple types of pending billable items are visible in the invoice drawer in QuickBooks Online. What does the Filter by option within the drawer allow the bookkeeper to accomplish?

answers.text: Sort all billable items alphabetically or by date so reviewing large lists is easier.
Narrow the items displayed in the drawer to a specific type, such as Time, Expenses, or Delayed Charges.
Restrict the drawer to show only items within a specific dollar amount range.
Automatically add all items of a selected type to the invoice without individual selection.

explanations.a: The Filter by option filters by item type, not sorts alphabetically or by date.
explanations.b: The Student Guide describes the Filter by option in the drawer as allowing the bookkeeper to narrow the displayed items to a specific type — such as Time, Expenses, or Delayed Charges — making it easier to manage large lists.
explanations.c: Filtering by dollar range is not the function of the Filter by drop-down in the drawer.
explanations.d: The Filter by option filters the displayed list; it does not automatically add all filtered items to the invoice. The Add all button performs that function.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: overpayment customer credit created future invoice
questions.text: A customer accidentally sends $100 more than the outstanding invoice balance. When the bookkeeper enters this overpayment amount in the Receive Payment screen, what does QuickBooks Online do?

answers.text: QBO automatically issues a Refund Receipt for the $100 overpayment without any bookkeeper action.
The $100 excess posts as a debit to the customer's AR, creating an open debit balance.
A credit of $100 is created for that customer in QBO, which can later be applied to a future invoice or refunded.
QBO rejects the entry and requires the bookkeeper to enter the exact invoice amount.

explanations.a: QBO does not automatically generate a Refund Receipt; the bookkeeper must intentionally create one if a cash refund is needed.
explanations.b: The overpayment creates a customer credit balance, not an AR debit balance; the credit can be applied to future invoices.
explanations.c: The Student Guide describes how an overpayment in Receive Payment results in a credit being stored for the customer, which can then be applied to a future invoice or converted to a Refund Receipt if cash is to be returned.
explanations.d: QBO does not reject overpayments; it accepts the amount and creates a credit for the difference.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.keyword: Refund Receipt reduces cash income accounts no AR
questions.text: When a Refund Receipt is created for a customer in QuickBooks Online, what is the correct description of its effect on the accounting records?

answers.text: It debits Accounts Receivable and credits the Income account, reversing the original revenue entry.
It credits Cash and debits Accounts Receivable, reducing both the cash and the AR balance simultaneously.
It creates a credit balance in the customer's AR sub-ledger without touching the bank or cash account.
It reduces Cash (credits the bank or payment account) and reduces Income (debits the Income account), decreasing both cash and revenue.

explanations.a: A Refund Receipt does not debit AR; it is used precisely when there is no AR balance, so cash goes directly back to the customer.
explanations.b: A Refund Receipt credits (reduces) Cash and debits Income, not Accounts Receivable; AR is not involved when a Refund Receipt is used.
explanations.c: A Refund Receipt does touch the bank or payment account by reducing cash; it is not a no-cash adjustment.
explanations.d: The Student Guide and QBO's transaction design show a Refund Receipt reduces the bank or payment account (credit to cash) and reduces revenue (debit to income), effectively reversing the original sales and cash receipt.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.1 Customer Center money bar — all segments
questions.keyword: Customer Center money bar Unbilled Overdue Open Paid segments
questions.text: The Customer Center money bar displays colored segments representing different states of customer activity. Which description correctly identifies the segments shown?

answers.text: Unbilled Activity, Overdue invoices, Open (not yet due) invoices, and recently Paid invoices.
Estimates, Open invoices, Overdue invoices, and Undeposited Funds.
Delayed Charges, Credit Memos, Open invoices, and Paid invoices.
Unbilled Activity, Open invoices, Accounts Receivable total, and Deposits in transit.

explanations.a: The Student Guide describes the Customer Center money bar as showing Unbilled Activity, Overdue, Open (not yet overdue), and recently Paid segments, which can be clicked to filter the customer transaction list.
explanations.b: Estimates and Undeposited Funds are not Customer Center money bar segments as described in the Student Guide.
explanations.c: Delayed Charges and Credit Memos are not named money bar segments in the Customer Center; they fall within Unbilled Activity.
explanations.d: Accounts Receivable total and Deposits in transit are not money bar segment names described in the Student Guide for the Customer Center.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.2 Projects vs. sub-customers — primary advantage of Projects
questions.keyword: Projects profit loss view income expenses labor costs engagement
questions.text: In QuickBooks Online, both the Projects feature and sub-customers can track income and expenses for a client engagement. What is the primary advantage of using Projects over sub-customers according to the Student Guide?

answers.text: Projects can be created without associating them with a parent customer, offering more flexible cost tracking.
Projects provide a dedicated profit and loss view for each engagement, showing income, costs, and labor together on a Project report.
Projects support inventory item tracking per job, while sub-customers do not support inventory.
Projects automatically convert to invoices when marked Complete, reducing manual billing steps.

explanations.a: Projects in QBO are associated with a customer; they are not free-standing cost centers unrelated to a client.
explanations.b: The Student Guide describes Projects as providing a dedicated project profitability view that shows income, expenses, and labor costs together, giving a clearer picture of per-engagement profitability compared to sub-customers.
explanations.c: Inventory tracking is not described as a differentiator between Projects and sub-customers in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: Projects do not automatically convert to invoices; invoicing is a separate step the bookkeeper initiates.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.6 Credit Memos — unapplied credit no open invoice
questions.keyword: Credit Memo unapplied credit no open invoice future invoice
questions.text: For a customer with no open invoices, a Credit Memo has been entered in QuickBooks Online. How does QBO handle the resulting credit on that customer's account?

answers.text: QBO automatically issues a Refund Receipt for the credit amount, returning cash to the customer immediately.
The credit is posted to a Credit Liability account and held until the customer requests application.
The credit remains as an unapplied credit on the customer's account and can be applied to a future invoice when one is created.
The credit expires after 30 days if not applied and must be re-entered as a new Credit Memo.

explanations.a: QBO does not automatically issue a Refund Receipt; a cash refund requires the bookkeeper to intentionally create a Refund Receipt transaction.
explanations.b: Credits are not posted to a Credit Liability account; they remain associated with the customer's AR record as an unapplied credit.
explanations.c: The Student Guide describes how a Credit Memo with no matching open invoice remains as an unapplied credit on the customer's account, ready to be applied when a future invoice is created.
explanations.d: QBO credits do not expire; they remain available indefinitely until applied to an invoice or converted to a refund.

questions.name: Customers & Sales Transactions
questions.objective: 5.11 Deposits — selecting payments from Undeposited Funds
questions.keyword: Deposit screen checkboxes select payments Undeposited Funds
questions.text: On the bank deposit screen in QuickBooks Online, which statement best describes how a bookkeeper selects which Undeposited Funds payments to include in the deposit?

answers.text: QBO automatically selects all items in Undeposited Funds and combines them into one deposit without allowing individual selection.
The bookkeeper must create a separate Deposit transaction for each payment to match individual bank lines.
The bookkeeper enters the bank statement ending balance and QBO automatically selects payments that equal that amount.
The bookkeeper checks boxes next to each payment to include in the deposit on the deposit screen, selecting only those that match the actual bank deposit.

explanations.a: QBO does not automatically select and commit all Undeposited Funds items; the bookkeeper must choose which payments to include by checking boxes.
explanations.b: Creating a separate deposit per payment defeats the purpose of Undeposited Funds and would not match single combined bank deposit lines.
explanations.c: QBO does not have an auto-match feature that selects payments to reach a target bank statement balance; that logic is part of the reconciliation process, not the deposit entry.
explanations.d: The Student Guide describes the deposit screen as presenting a list of all payments in Undeposited Funds with checkboxes, allowing the bookkeeper to select exactly which payments to include in the current deposit to match the actual bank deposit amount.
